note: Reusable constructions. An archetype is how an item is built, never its topic.

archetypes.label: radical over a power product rewritten in rational-exponent form
archetypes.given: a radical of fixed index over a product of powers
archetypes.find: an equivalent expression in another notation
archetypes.transformation: divide each exponent by the index, or move the index into the exponent
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the index divides every exponent in the radicand, including those equal to 1
archetypes.wrong_route: divide only the first factor, or invert index and exponent
archetypes.distractor_basis: index/exponent inverted, or the root applied to part of the radicand only
archetypes.cognitive_demand: holding one operation across every factor while the notation changes

archetypes.label: two radical expressions asserted equivalent, an exponent parameter recovered
archetypes.given: two radical expressions of different bases declared equivalent, plus a target of the form base^(linear in the parameter)
archetypes.transformation: convert both sides to rational exponents, equate, then solve a linear equation in the parameter
archetypes.hidden_relationship: equivalence of the two radicals forces a relation between the two bases before the parameter can be reached
archetypes.wrong_route: equate the radicands or the indices directly instead of the rational exponents
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable in student-produced form; the wrong route yields a plausible fraction
archetypes.cognitive_demand: a two-stage reversal: relate the bases, then invert the target expression

archetypes.label: product of radicals of one base collapsed to a single power, the exponent asked
archetypes.given: a product or quotient of radicals sharing a base
archetypes.find: the exponent parameter of an asserted equivalent single power
archetypes.transformation: sum the rational exponents, then equate to the target exponent and solve
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the asked quantity sits inside the exponent of the target form, so the sum is not the answer
archetypes.wrong_route: report the summed exponent instead of solving for the parameter
archetypes.distractor_basis: student-produced; the unsolved sum is the natural wrong answer
archetypes.cognitive_demand: completing an extra inversion after the visible work is done

archetypes.label: monomials multiplied where the asked quantity is the coefficient, not the exponent
archetypes.given: a product of monomials with an asserted equivalent single term
archetypes.transformation: multiply coefficients and add exponents, then read off the requested part
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the exponent work is visible and irrelevant; the coefficient is the target
archetypes.wrong_route: report the exponent, which the working makes salient
archetypes.distractor_basis: student-produced; the exponent is the competing answer
archetypes.cognitive_demand: target discipline — resisting the quantity the working foregrounds

archetypes.label: power and negative-exponent rules applied across a product to select an equivalent form
archetypes.given: a product or quotient of powers, possibly with negative exponents
archetypes.transformation: add exponents on like bases, distribute an outer power, resolve negative exponents
archetypes.hidden_relationship: none; the demand is uniform application without slips
archetypes.wrong_route: multiply exponents where they should be added, or drop a sign
archetypes.distractor_basis: each option encodes one specific rule slip — added vs multiplied exponents, sign of a negative exponent
archetypes.cognitive_demand: sustained accuracy across several bases at once

archetypes.label: a literal equation solved for a variable trapped under a radical or square
archetypes.given: an equation relating several literals, one of them inside a radical or squared
archetypes.find: an equivalent equation expressing that variable in terms of the others
archetypes.transformation: square or root both sides, then isolate, preserving the whole side through each step
archetypes.hidden_relationship: squaring acts on the entire side, not term by term
archetypes.wrong_route: square or root term by term, or isolate before undoing the radical
archetypes.distractor_basis: options differ by whether the operation was applied to the whole side and by the order of the two moves
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reversal against the direction the equation is written in

archetypes.label: the y-intercept read from an exponential written in initial-value form
archetypes.given: an exponential function in the form coefficient times base to the x, possibly plus a constant
archetypes.find: the y-intercept or the value at zero
archetypes.transformation: substitute zero and use that any base to the zero is one
archetypes.hidden_relationship: none when the form is plain; the base term vanishes
archetypes.wrong_route: read off a printed constant without substituting
archetypes.distractor_basis: every printed constant appears as an option, so guessing by appearance lands on one
archetypes.cognitive_demand: one substitution; the difficulty is entirely in the printed decoys

archetypes.label: an intercept asked of a transformed graph, so the printed constant is not the answer
archetypes.given: a function with unknown constants and a condition on the graph of a shifted or reflected version
archetypes.transformation: express the stated intercept as the transformed value at zero, then solve with the second condition
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the stated intercept belongs to the transformed graph, not to the function as written
archetypes.wrong_route: treat the stated intercept as the value of the original function at zero
archetypes.distractor_basis: student-produced; the untransformed reading gives a clean wrong number
archetypes.cognitive_demand: noticing a transformation that the question states only in passing

archetypes.label: the parameters of an exponential recovered from two stated conditions
archetypes.given: a function of the form a to the x plus b with two stated points or a point and a product
archetypes.find: a parameter or a combination of them
archetypes.transformation: turn each condition into an equation, then solve the pair
archetypes.hidden_relationship: one condition usually fixes the additive constant, freeing the other
archetypes.wrong_route: use one condition only, or substitute into the wrong slot
archetypes.distractor_basis: student-produced; partial use of the conditions yields a near answer
archetypes.cognitive_demand: coordinating two constraints rather than executing one

archetypes.label: choosing which equivalent form displays a named quantity as a constant or coefficient
archetypes.given: two or more algebraically equivalent forms of one exponential, and a named feature
archetypes.find: which forms show that feature explicitly
archetypes.transformation: evaluate the feature for each candidate and check whether it appears literally
archetypes.hidden_relationship: equivalence is assumed, so the question is about display, not about value
archetypes.wrong_route: pick the form that merely looks simplest, or compute the value and match a numeral
archetypes.distractor_basis: the Roman-numeral frame makes every subset a printed option, so a half-check still lands somewhere
archetypes.cognitive_demand: separating what an expression equals from what it shows

archetypes.label: the leading coefficient of a contextual exponential interpreted in words
archetypes.given: a fitted exponential in a described context
archetypes.transformation: identify the coefficient as the value at time zero and restate it in the context
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the coefficient is the initial value, not a rate, and not an extreme over the interval
archetypes.wrong_route: read it as a rate of change, a percentage, or the value at the end of the stated interval
archetypes.distractor_basis: options offer rate, percentage, and end-of-interval readings of the same number
archetypes.cognitive_demand: translation between the algebraic role of a parameter and its meaning in the situation

archetypes.label: a stated function value interpreted as a sentence about the context
archetypes.given: a contextual exponential and a numerical statement about one evaluation
archetypes.find: the correct reading of that statement
archetypes.transformation: map input to the context variable and output to the modelled quantity
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the roles of input and output are swappable in the options and must be held apart
archetypes.wrong_route: exchange the input and output, or attach the wrong unit to one of them
archetypes.distractor_basis: options systematically swap the two numbers and their units
archetypes.cognitive_demand: holding a two-way correspondence while reading fluent prose

archetypes.label: a growth factor re-expressed over a different period
archetypes.given: an exponential whose exponent carries a divisor or multiplier setting the compounding period
archetypes.find: the period, the percentage, or an equivalent function on another time unit
archetypes.transformation: set the exponent structures equal and solve for the period or rate
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the divisor in the exponent is a unit conversion, not part of the growth factor
archetypes.wrong_route: read the divisor as the rate, or convert in the wrong direction
archetypes.distractor_basis: options include the divisor itself, its reciprocal, and the base minus one
archetypes.cognitive_demand: seeing the exponent as carrying units as well as size

archetypes.label: an exponential model assembled from a verbal percentage description
archetypes.given: an initial amount and a per-period percentage increase or decrease in words
archetypes.transformation: convert the percentage to a growth factor and place initial value and factor in their slots
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a percentage change becomes one plus or minus the decimal, not the decimal itself
archetypes.wrong_route: use the bare decimal as the base, or swap initial value and base
archetypes.distractor_basis: options cover base-versus-coefficient swaps and the decimal-versus-one-plus-decimal confusion
archetypes.cognitive_demand: building structure from prose rather than manipulating given structure

archetypes.label: an exponential recovered from tabulated values
archetypes.given: a short table of inputs and outputs stated to be exponential
archetypes.transformation: read the value at zero as the coefficient and a ratio of consecutive outputs as the base
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the base is a ratio, not a difference, and the table may not start at zero
archetypes.wrong_route: take successive differences, giving a linear model
archetypes.distractor_basis: options include the linear reading and coefficient/base swaps
archetypes.cognitive_demand: recognising multiplicative structure in a small numeric table

archetypes.label: a feature of an exponential read from a described or drawn curve
archetypes.given: a graph of an exponential, described by its trend and points
archetypes.find: an intercept, an asymptote, or an interpretation
archetypes.transformation: locate the feature on the curve and read its value
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the horizontal asymptote is the additive constant, not zero, when the curve is shifted
archetypes.wrong_route: read a nearby plotted point instead of the exact intercept
archetypes.distractor_basis: options include neighbouring plotted values and the asymptote
archetypes.cognitive_demand: moving between a visual feature and its algebraic name

archetypes.label: a new function formed by shifting the input or output of an exponential
archetypes.given: an exponential and a definition of a second function by a shift
archetypes.find: the explicit form of the second
archetypes.transformation: substitute the shifted argument and fold the resulting constant factor into the coefficient
archetypes.hidden_relationship: an input shift multiplies the coefficient by a power of the base; an output shift does not
archetypes.wrong_route: add the shift to the coefficient, or apply an input shift as an output shift
archetypes.distractor_basis: options separate the two shift types and the add-versus-multiply confusion
archetypes.cognitive_demand: knowing which part of the form a transformation reaches

archetypes.label: an exponential evaluated or compared at given inputs
archetypes.given: a function and one or more inputs
archetypes.find: an output, or the input matching an output
archetypes.transformation: substitute and compute, or match against a supplied table or graph
archetypes.hidden_relationship: none; the work is direct
archetypes.wrong_route: mis-apply a negative or fractional exponent
archetypes.distractor_basis: options encode sign and reciprocal slips on the exponent
archetypes.cognitive_demand: accuracy under exponent rules rather than any inference

archetypes.label: construction not determinable from the extracted source
archetypes.given: UNKNOWN
archetypes.transformation: UNKNOWN
archetypes.hidden_relationship: UNKNOWN
archetypes.wrong_route: UNKNOWN
archetypes.distractor_basis: UNKNOWN
archetypes.cognitive_demand: UNKNOWN — the item carries a figure or expression the text layer did not preserve

archetypes.label: a quadratic-shaped expression rewritten as a product of two binomials
archetypes.given: a trinomial, possibly quadratic in a power of the variable rather than in the variable
archetypes.transformation: find the pair whose product is the constant term and whose sum is the linear coefficient
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the sum condition and the product condition must hold at the same time, so one alone never identifies the pair
archetypes.wrong_route: satisfy the product and ignore the sum, or attach the signs to the wrong member of the pair
archetypes.distractor_basis: pairs with the right product and the wrong sum, and the right pair with swapped signs
archetypes.cognitive_demand: holding two simultaneous conditions on one pair of numbers

archetypes.label: one factor of a polynomial selected from printed candidates
archetypes.given: a polynomial that shares a common factor or factors over the integers
archetypes.transformation: extract the common factor, or factor fully and match against the options
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a numeric common factor is a factor as much as a binomial is, which the option set exploits
archetypes.wrong_route: read a term of the polynomial as a factor of it
archetypes.distractor_basis: terms of the original expression offered as factors
archetypes.cognitive_demand: separating the notion of a term from the notion of a factor

archetypes.label: which of four polynomials admits a stated parameterised factor
archetypes.given: four trinomials differing only in the linear coefficient, and a factor written with a symbolic constant
archetypes.find: the one for which the factorisation is consistent
archetypes.transformation: set the stated factor against the general factorisation and solve the coefficient condition
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the constant term fixes the second factor, so only one linear coefficient can survive
archetypes.wrong_route: test the constant term only, or match the linear coefficient by inspection
archetypes.distractor_basis: linear coefficients reachable by pairing the wrong divisors of the constant term
archetypes.cognitive_demand: working a factorisation backwards with a symbol standing in for a number

archetypes.label: x-intercepts stated, a true statement about the function chosen
archetypes.given: the x-intercepts of a polynomial graph
archetypes.find: which equation about the function must be true
archetypes.transformation: read an intercept as an input whose output is zero
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the ordinate of an x-intercept is zero, so the abscissa is the input and never the output
archetypes.wrong_route: feed zero to the function and expect an intercept back, or swap the coordinates
archetypes.distractor_basis: coordinates transposed, and the intercept read as a function value
archetypes.cognitive_demand: keeping input and output straight when both are printed as one pair

archetypes.label: a point on the graph given, the function value at that input asked
archetypes.given: one point the graph passes through
archetypes.find: the value of the function at the point s abscissa
archetypes.transformation: read the ordinate
archetypes.hidden_relationship: there is nothing to compute; the pair already states the answer
archetypes.wrong_route: return the abscissa, or combine the two coordinates
archetypes.distractor_basis: the abscissa, the sum, and the product of the coordinates
archetypes.cognitive_demand: resisting the expectation that a question must be worked

archetypes.label: a factored polynomial with an unknown constant, pinned by a stated root, then evaluated elsewhere
archetypes.given: a product of linear factors, one carrying an unknown constant, and a point on the graph
archetypes.find: the value of the function at a different input
archetypes.transformation: use the stated root to recover the constant, then evaluate
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the given point is a root, so it fixes the constant before any evaluation is possible
archetypes.wrong_route: evaluate with the constant left symbolic, or stop once the constant is found
archetypes.distractor_basis: the recovered constant itself, and the product of the printed constants
archetypes.cognitive_demand: a two-stage solve where the first stage looks like the answer

archetypes.label: a parameterised factored equation whose roots satisfy a stated sum or product
archetypes.given: a product of factors set to zero, one factor pair built from a radical in the parameter
archetypes.transformation: list the roots, form the stated symmetric function, and solve
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the conjugate pair contributes a product that is the negated radicand, not the radicand
archetypes.wrong_route: omit the root contributed by the leading linear factor, or take the conjugate product with the wrong sign
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: assembling a symmetric function of roots without solving for each root numerically

archetypes.label: a fully factored equation, one root singled out by a stated property
archetypes.given: a product of several linear factors set to zero
archetypes.find: the root with the stated sign
archetypes.transformation: read each root off its factor and select
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a factor written with a negated leading coefficient still contributes a root of the opposite sign
archetypes.wrong_route: read the constant inside a factor as the root without negating
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: sign discipline across several factors written in different orders

archetypes.label: a cubic with a common monomial factor, the smallest constant in a linear factor asked
archetypes.given: a cubic that factors as a monomial times a quadratic, and a factor written in a stated form
archetypes.find: the smallest constant fitting that form
archetypes.transformation: remove the monomial factor, factor the quadratic, and compare the two constants
archetypes.hidden_relationship: both constants fit the stated form, so the question is a comparison rather than a factorisation
archetypes.wrong_route: stop at the first factor found, or report the larger constant
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: finishing a factorisation that already yields a usable answer partway

archetypes.label: the largest middle coefficient for which a disguised quadratic factors over the integers
archetypes.given: a trinomial in a power of the variable with an unknown middle coefficient and a stated factor form
archetypes.find: the greatest value the middle coefficient can take
archetypes.transformation: enumerate the integer factor pairs of the outer coefficients and maximise the resulting cross term
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the extreme value comes from the most lopsided pairing, not the most balanced one
archetypes.wrong_route: take the balanced pairing, or add the outer coefficients directly
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: searching a small space for an extremum rather than solving an equation

archetypes.label: a product of two shifted squares pinned by two points, then a symmetric pair of values summed
archetypes.given: a function built as a scalar times two differences of a shifted square and a constant, and two points on its graph
archetypes.find: the sum of the function at two inputs placed symmetrically about the shift
archetypes.transformation: recover the constants from the two conditions, then exploit the symmetry of the shift
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the two asked inputs are mirror images about the shift, so they share a value and the sum is a doubling
archetypes.wrong_route: solve both constants separately and evaluate twice, missing the symmetry and the arithmetic with it
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: noticing a symmetry that turns a long computation into a short one

archetypes.label: the sign of a factored cubic on an interval, with candidate locations tested
archetypes.given: a cubic in fully factored form with ordered unknown roots and its sign on one interval
archetypes.find: which of several candidate locations for a point of stated sign could hold
archetypes.transformation: propagate the sign across the roots and test each candidate interval
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the stated sign on one interval fixes the sign on every other interval, so one datum settles all three claims
archetypes.wrong_route: assume the leading coefficient sets the sign on the leftmost interval, ignoring the stated one
archetypes.distractor_basis: option sets built from the intervals of the wrong sign, singly and in pairs
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reasoning about sign changes without any numbers to evaluate

archetypes.label: a vertical translation applied to a factored polynomial, then evaluated at a point
archetypes.given: a product of linear factors and a stated vertical shift
archetypes.find: the value of the translated function at one input
archetypes.transformation: evaluate the original and add the shift
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a vertical shift adds to the output and leaves the input untouched
archetypes.wrong_route: shift the input instead of the output, or subtract the shift
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: applying a transformation on the correct axis

archetypes.label: a common binomial factor extracted from a difference, then a parameter recovered from a stated root
archetypes.given: an equation whose two sides share a binomial factor, with two symbolic constants and one stated root
archetypes.transformation: factor the shared binomial out, discard the root it contributes, and solve the remaining factor at the stated root
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the stated root belongs to the other factor, so the shared binomial cannot be used to find the parameter
archetypes.wrong_route: substitute the stated root into the shared binomial and solve for the wrong constant
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: deciding which factor a given root came from

archetypes.label: a rational function formed by dividing out one root, its remaining intercepts counted
archetypes.given: the number of x-intercepts of a function and one named intercept, and a quotient by the corresponding linear factor
archetypes.find: how many x-intercepts the quotient has
archetypes.transformation: cancel the named root and count what remains
archetypes.hidden_relationship: dividing by the factor removes exactly that intercept and leaves the rest, provided its multiplicity is one
archetypes.wrong_route: count the original intercepts, or assume the division removes more than one
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reasoning about a count under an operation rather than computing the objects

archetypes.label: an expression built from sums and products expanded to an equivalent standard form
archetypes.given: a combination of polynomial terms, products or squares
archetypes.transformation: distribute, then collect like terms
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a subtraction distributes across every term of what follows it, not only the first
archetypes.wrong_route: distribute the leading sign over one term only, or add exponents when adding terms
archetypes.distractor_basis: one distributed sign dropped, one like-term pair mishandled, and both
archetypes.cognitive_demand: sustained sign and bookkeeping accuracy over several terms

archetypes.label: two like terms combined, where the exponent invites the same operation as the coefficient
archetypes.given: a sum or difference of two monomials of equal degree
archetypes.transformation: operate on the coefficients and leave the exponent alone
archetypes.hidden_relationship: combining like terms is addition of coefficients; the exponent is an index, not a quantity
archetypes.wrong_route: multiply the coefficients, or apply the operation to the exponent as well
archetypes.distractor_basis: coefficients multiplied, exponents added, and both
archetypes.cognitive_demand: holding the exponent fixed while the coefficient moves

archetypes.label: the greatest common factor extracted from a polynomial of several terms
archetypes.given: a polynomial whose terms share numeric and variable factors
archetypes.transformation: take the largest numeric divisor and the least power present of each shared variable
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the least power present, not the greatest, is what every term contains
archetypes.wrong_route: pull out a factor that only some terms carry, or leave a term with no factor at all
archetypes.distractor_basis: the wrong numeric divisor, the wrong power extracted, and a bracket that fails to reconstitute one term
archetypes.cognitive_demand: choosing the extreme in the right direction across every term

archetypes.label: two forms asserted equivalent, a coefficient or parameter recovered by matching
archetypes.given: an expression and an equivalent form carrying one or more symbolic constants
archetypes.find: a constant, or a stated combination of them
archetypes.transformation: expand one side and equate coefficients of like powers
archetypes.hidden_relationship: equivalence for all inputs is stronger than agreement at a point, and forces every coefficient to match
archetypes.wrong_route: match one coefficient and stop, or report a single constant when a combination was asked
archetypes.distractor_basis: individual constants offered where their product or sum was asked
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reading what was asked after the hard part is finished

archetypes.label: a quadratic rewritten as a shifted square plus a constant
archetypes.given: a quadratic in standard form
archetypes.transformation: halve the linear coefficient, square it, and compensate
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the compensating constant is subtracted, so the free term moves by the square of the half-coefficient
archetypes.wrong_route: negate the shift, or add the compensating constant instead of subtracting it
archetypes.distractor_basis: the shift sign flipped, the compensation sign flipped, and both
archetypes.cognitive_demand: tracking two independent sign decisions in one rewrite

archetypes.label: a rational expression reduced by cancelling a shared factor
archetypes.given: a quotient whose numerator and denominator share a factor, with a domain restriction stated
archetypes.transformation: factor both parts and cancel what is common
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the stated restriction is what makes the cancellation legitimate rather than incidental
archetypes.wrong_route: cancel a term rather than a factor, or expand instead of factoring
archetypes.distractor_basis: the unreduced expansion, a term cancelled illegitimately, and a partial reduction
archetypes.cognitive_demand: seeing a common factor inside an expression written expanded

archetypes.label: rational expressions combined over a common denominator
archetypes.given: a sum or difference of two rational expressions with unlike denominators
archetypes.find: the single equivalent expression, or a constant in its numerator
archetypes.transformation: cross-multiply onto the common denominator and collect the numerator
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the subtraction distributes over the whole second numerator once it is expanded
archetypes.wrong_route: add numerators and denominators separately, or drop a sign in the second numerator
archetypes.distractor_basis: numerators combined without the common denominator, and one sign dropped
archetypes.cognitive_demand: two levels of bookkeeping at once, above and below the bar

archetypes.label: a quotient that divides exactly, the resulting coefficients asked
archetypes.given: a quadratic over a linear factor asserted equal to a linear form with symbolic coefficients
archetypes.find: a coefficient of the quotient, or a stated combination of them
archetypes.transformation: factor the numerator, cancel the divisor, and read the quotient off
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the divisor is a factor of the numerator, so nothing survives the division and long division is never needed
archetypes.wrong_route: divide term by term, or assume a remainder the exact division does not leave
archetypes.distractor_basis: combinations formed from the numerator constants rather than the quotient
archetypes.cognitive_demand: seeing that the division closes rather than starting an algorithm

archetypes.label: a quotient that does not divide exactly, rewritten as a polynomial plus a remainder term
archetypes.given: a quadratic over a linear expression that is not a factor of it
archetypes.transformation: divide, then carry the remainder over the original divisor
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the remainder is the difference between the numerator and the product the quotient reconstructs, and it keeps the original denominator
archetypes.wrong_route: take a quotient one step short, or compute the remainder against the wrong product
archetypes.distractor_basis: the right quotient with the wrong remainder, and the wrong quotient with a plausible one
archetypes.cognitive_demand: carrying two results out of one division and keeping them attached correctly

archetypes.label: a product that collapses because all but two terms cancel
archetypes.given: a binomial times a long geometric-looking sum
archetypes.transformation: distribute and observe that consecutive terms annihilate in pairs
archetypes.hidden_relationship: only the first and last terms survive, so the degree of the answer is one more than the highest printed power
archetypes.wrong_route: count the terms in the sum and use that count as the surviving exponent
archetypes.distractor_basis: exponents one above and one below the surviving one
archetypes.cognitive_demand: trusting a cancellation across a long expression rather than expanding it

archetypes.label: a stated factor used as a root to recover a parameter
archetypes.given: an expression with a symbolic parameter and the assertion that a named linear expression divides it
archetypes.transformation: set the stated factor to zero and substitute that value into the expression
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a factor supplies a root, so the whole expression must vanish there whatever the other symbols are
archetypes.wrong_route: match coefficients as if the factorisation were known, or invert the fraction the parameter sits under
archetypes.distractor_basis: the parameter reciprocated, negated, and both
archetypes.cognitive_demand: converting a divisibility statement into an evaluation

archetypes.label: a rational exponent rewritten as a radical, where index and radicand must move together
archetypes.given: a power with a fractional exponent
archetypes.transformation: read the denominator as the index and the numerator as the inner power, scaling both if the printed radicand is already fixed
archetypes.hidden_relationship: multiplying the inner exponent by a factor requires multiplying the index by the same factor
archetypes.wrong_route: take the index from the numerator, or scale the radicand without scaling the index
archetypes.distractor_basis: index and inner exponent exchanged, and indices that scale by the wrong factor
archetypes.cognitive_demand: keeping a ratio invariant while both of its parts change

archetypes.label: a two-by-two system solved, then a stated linear combination of the unknowns evaluated
archetypes.given: two linear equations in two unknowns and an expression in those unknowns
archetypes.transformation: eliminate one unknown, back-substitute, then substitute both into the asked expression
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the asked combination is often a scalar multiple of the sum or difference of the two equations, so the solve can be skipped entirely
archetypes.wrong_route: stop at one unknown, or report the solution instead of the combination
archetypes.distractor_basis: each unknown on its own, and the combination formed with one sign wrong
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reading what was asked after the hard part is finished

archetypes.label: the system and the question are both built on a compound expression, which is the real unknown
archetypes.given: two equations whose terms are grouped, and a question about the same grouping
archetypes.find: the value of the grouped expression
archetypes.transformation: add or subtract the equations so the grouping survives and its partner cancels
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the individual variables never need to be found, and finding them is the long way round
archetypes.wrong_route: expand the groupings and solve for each variable separately
archetypes.distractor_basis: the ungrouped variable, and the grouping scaled by the wrong factor
archetypes.cognitive_demand: treating a compound expression as a single object

archetypes.label: a system solved and the solution reported as an ordered pair
archetypes.given: two linear equations, often one already solved for a variable
archetypes.transformation: substitute or eliminate, then pair the two values
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the order of the pair is part of the answer, and the options exploit reversing it
archetypes.wrong_route: transpose the coordinates, or solve for one variable and pair it with a printed constant

archetypes.cognitive_demand: carrying two values without confusing which is which

archetypes.label: a system solved and one coordinate reported
archetypes.given: two linear equations in two unknowns
archetypes.transformation: eliminate the other unknown
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the other coordinate is often easier to reach, so the item punishes answering the question it was easier to answer
archetypes.wrong_route: report the other coordinate
archetypes.distractor_basis: the other coordinate, and coefficients printed in the equations
archetypes.cognitive_demand: finishing on the asked variable rather than the convenient one

archetypes.label: one equation given, a second chosen so the system is inconsistent
archetypes.given: one linear equation and four candidate partners
archetypes.find: the partner making the system inconsistent
archetypes.transformation: match the coefficient ratio and break the constant ratio
archetypes.hidden_relationship: parallel means the same slope AND a different intercept; matching all three ratios makes the system dependent instead
archetypes.wrong_route: choose the candidate proportional in every term, which gives infinitely many solutions rather than none
archetypes.distractor_basis: the fully proportional candidate, and candidates with the wrong slope
archetypes.cognitive_demand: holding two conditions, one to satisfy and one to violate

archetypes.label: one equation given, a second chosen so the system has exactly one solution
archetypes.given: one linear equation and four candidate partners
archetypes.find: the partner making the system consistent and independent
archetypes.transformation: reject every candidate whose coefficients are proportional to the given one
archetypes.hidden_relationship: exactly one solution is the DEFAULT, so the work is elimination of the proportional candidates rather than construction
archetypes.wrong_route: look for a property the correct answer does not need to have
archetypes.distractor_basis: candidates proportional in the coefficients, in one term only, or in all terms
archetypes.cognitive_demand: recognising a question whose answer is defined by what it is not

archetypes.label: a printed system classified by how many solutions it has
archetypes.given: two or three equations
archetypes.transformation: compare coefficient ratios; with three equations, check every pair
archetypes.hidden_relationship: three equations are consistent only if all three concur, so one contradictory pair settles it
archetypes.wrong_route: check one pair and generalise, or read proportional coefficients as proportional constants
archetypes.distractor_basis: the count that follows from checking only part of the system
archetypes.cognitive_demand: knowing how many comparisons the question actually requires

archetypes.label: the system with a stated solution count selected from four printed systems
archetypes.given: four two-equation systems
archetypes.find: the one matching the stated count
archetypes.transformation: test the coefficient and constant ratios of each
archetypes.hidden_relationship: no solution and infinitely many differ only in whether the constant ratio matches, so the two are one step apart
archetypes.wrong_route: stop at the coefficient ratio and not check the constants
archetypes.distractor_basis: the system with the other degenerate behaviour, and systems that are simply independent
archetypes.cognitive_demand: a ratio test applied four times without losing track

archetypes.label: a parameter chosen so the system has a stated solution count
archetypes.given: two equations, one carrying an unknown constant, and a stated count
archetypes.transformation: set the coefficient ratios equal and solve for the constant
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the scale factor is fixed by the terms that carry no parameter, so the parameter is determined before it is solved for
archetypes.wrong_route: match the wrong pair of terms, or read the scale factor off the constants
archetypes.distractor_basis: the scale factor itself, and the parameter from the wrong pairing
archetypes.cognitive_demand: finding the scale factor before using it

archetypes.label: a parameter recovered from a stated intersection point
archetypes.given: two equations carrying constants and a point where their graphs meet, one coordinate of which may be unnamed
archetypes.transformation: substitute the known coordinate into both equations and eliminate the unknown coordinate between them
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the unknown coordinate cancels between the two equations, so it never needs finding
archetypes.wrong_route: try to find the unnamed coordinate first, or substitute into one equation only
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable where the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: eliminating an unknown you were never asked about

archetypes.label: a dependent system, and the parametric point that lies on both graphs
archetypes.given: two equations that are scalar multiples of each other, and a free real parameter
archetypes.transformation: solve the single underlying equation for one variable in terms of the parameter
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the two equations are one equation, so the solution set is a line and the parameter is a coordinate of it
archetypes.wrong_route: place the parameter in the wrong coordinate, or solve for the other variable
archetypes.distractor_basis: the pair with its coordinates transposed, the reciprocal slope, and points built from the unreduced equation
archetypes.cognitive_demand: describing a solution set rather than a solution

archetypes.label: a described situation turned into the system that represents it
archetypes.given: a verbal situation with two quantities and two conditions
archetypes.transformation: name the quantities, then write one equation per stated condition
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a ratio condition and a total condition are different shapes, and swapping which is which produces a printed option
archetypes.wrong_route: attach each rate to the wrong quantity, or make the total the weighted equation
archetypes.distractor_basis: the two rates exchanged, and the two conditions exchanged
archetypes.cognitive_demand: translating without solving

archetypes.label: a described situation solved for one quantity
archetypes.given: a verbal situation with two quantities, two conditions, and one quantity fixed
archetypes.transformation: build the equations, substitute the fixed quantity, and solve
archetypes.hidden_relationship: one condition is often already numeric, so the system collapses to a single equation
archetypes.wrong_route: solve for the quantity that was given, or drop a unit rate
archetypes.distractor_basis: the fixed quantity, and results from omitting one term of the total
archetypes.cognitive_demand: building and finishing in one pass

archetypes.label: the solution of a system read off a plotted pair of lines
archetypes.given: a graph of two lines
archetypes.transformation: read the crossing point
archetypes.hidden_relationship: nothing is computed; the answer is a reading, and the options are the other coordinate and nearby lattice values
archetypes.wrong_route: read the other coordinate, or read an intercept instead of the intersection
archetypes.distractor_basis: the other coordinate, and the intercepts of each line
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reading a plot accurately under the expectation that something must be solved

archetypes.label: an equation added to a plotted system, and the solution count of the result
archetypes.given: a graph of two lines and a third equation in symbols
archetypes.find: how many solutions the three-equation system has
archetypes.transformation: locate the plotted intersection and test the third equation at it
archetypes.hidden_relationship: three equations are consistent only if the third passes through the existing intersection, so the count is almost always zero
archetypes.wrong_route: count the pairwise intersections of three lines
archetypes.distractor_basis: the pairwise count, and the count for a concurrent system
archetypes.cognitive_demand: moving between a plotted pair and a symbolic third

archetypes.label: the parameters of an unplotted line recovered from a plotted one under a stated solution count
archetypes.given: a plotted line and a second line written with symbolic coefficients, plus a stated count
archetypes.find: a combination of the symbolic coefficients, or a value they cannot take
archetypes.transformation: read the plotted line, scale it to match the printed leading coefficient, and read the remaining constants off
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the printed leading coefficient fixes the scale factor, so every other constant follows from the plot
archetypes.wrong_route: read the plotted line without scaling, or scale by the wrong term
archetypes.distractor_basis: values reachable by the same scaling of a different reading of the plot
archetypes.cognitive_demand: combining a measured reading with an algebraic scaling

archetypes.label: a feature of the unseen second equation of a dependent system
archetypes.given: one equation in slope-intercept form and the statement that the system has infinitely many solutions
archetypes.find: the slope or the intercept of the other equation
archetypes.transformation: recognise that the two equations describe the same line
archetypes.hidden_relationship: infinitely many solutions means one line, so the asked feature is simply copied from the printed equation
archetypes.wrong_route: take the negative reciprocal, as for a perpendicular, or negate the intercept
archetypes.distractor_basis: the negative reciprocal, the reciprocal, and the negated value
archetypes.cognitive_demand: resisting the pull of the perpendicular-slope rule

archetypes.label: a linear and a non-linear equation, the number of intersections asked
archetypes.given: a parabola and a horizontal or oblique line
archetypes.find: how many solutions the system has
archetypes.transformation: compare the line against the vertex, or set the two equal and count real roots
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the vertex decides it, so the discriminant never has to be computed
archetypes.wrong_route: assume two intersections because a parabola meets a line twice
archetypes.distractor_basis: the counts for a line above, at, and below the vertex
archetypes.cognitive_demand: locating a vertex without graphing

archetypes.label: a linear and a non-linear equation solved, and a value of the solution asked
archetypes.given: a parabola and a line
archetypes.find: a coordinate, or a combination of the coordinates, at an intersection
archetypes.transformation: substitute the line into the curve, solve the resulting quadratic, and evaluate
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the item says "a possible value", so either root is acceptable and only one appears among the options
archetypes.wrong_route: take the other root and expect it to be printed, or stop at the root instead of the asked combination
archetypes.distractor_basis: the roots themselves, and the combination formed from the wrong root
archetypes.cognitive_demand: carrying a quadratic solve through to a compound answer

archetypes.label: candidate partner equations tested for consistency, as Roman numerals
archetypes.given: one equation and two numbered candidates
archetypes.find: which candidates leave the system with at least one solution
archetypes.transformation: test each candidate for proportionality of coefficients and constants
archetypes.hidden_relationship: "at least one solution" admits both the independent and the dependent case, so only the inconsistent candidate fails
archetypes.wrong_route: read "at least one" as "exactly one" and reject the dependent candidate
archetypes.distractor_basis: the option set covering each candidate alone, both, and neither
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reading a quantifier precisely

archetypes.label: a feature read directly off a circle written in centre-radius form
archetypes.given: a circle in standard form
archetypes.transformation: read the shifts and take the square root of the constant
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the printed shift is the NEGATIVE of the coordinate, and the printed constant is the square of the radius
archetypes.wrong_route: copy the printed shifts unchanged, or report the constant as the radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: both signs flipped, one sign flipped, and the unrooted constant
archetypes.cognitive_demand: two independent sign decisions and one root, on an item that looks like a reading

archetypes.label: a circle in general form completed to standard form, then a derived length asked
archetypes.given: a circle as an expanded quadratic equal to zero, and a figure built on it
archetypes.find: a length of the surrounding figure
archetypes.transformation: complete the square in both variables, take the radius, then build the asked length
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a circle inscribed in a square makes the square side the DIAMETER, not the radius
archetypes.wrong_route: use the radius as the side, or stop at the radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: the perimeter built from the radius, from the diameter squared, and the unrooted constant
archetypes.cognitive_demand: chaining a completion of the square into a geometric relation

archetypes.label: a circle given by centre and radius, expanded, and one general-form coefficient asked
archetypes.given: a centre, a radius, and the general form with named coefficients
archetypes.transformation: write the standard form, expand, and collect the constant term
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the constant term is the sum of the squared shifts minus the squared radius, so all three inputs reach it
archetypes.wrong_route: report the squared radius, or drop one squared shift
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: expanding accurately when only one coefficient is wanted

archetypes.label: whether a point lies on a circle, or which coordinate is possible
archetypes.given: a circle in standard form and candidate points or a partial coordinate
archetypes.find: the point that satisfies the equation, or a possible coordinate
archetypes.transformation: substitute and test, or bound the coordinate by the centre and radius
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a coordinate is possible exactly when it lies within one radius of the centre
archetypes.wrong_route: test the centre, or use the radius squared as the reach
archetypes.distractor_basis: the centre itself, its reflection, and coordinates one radius-squared away
archetypes.cognitive_demand: substitution, or an interval argument in place of one

archetypes.label: a circle translated, and the equation of the image
archetypes.given: a circle in standard form and a translation
archetypes.find: the equation of the translated circle
archetypes.transformation: shift the relevant coordinate and leave the radius alone
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a horizontal shift changes only the x term, and the printed shift moves the opposite way to the sign
archetypes.wrong_route: shift the wrong coordinate, shift the wrong way, or change the radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: the other coordinate shifted, the shift applied with the wrong sign, and the radius altered
archetypes.cognitive_demand: applying one change and resisting three others

archetypes.label: a concentric circle with a scaled radius, and the new constant
archetypes.given: a circle in standard form and a radius scaled or offset
archetypes.find: the constant on the right-hand side of the new equation
archetypes.transformation: take the radius, transform it, and square the result
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the printed constant is the radius SQUARED, so scaling the radius by k scales it by k squared
archetypes.wrong_route: scale the constant directly, or add the offset to the constant
archetypes.distractor_basis: the constant scaled linearly, and the offset applied before the square
archetypes.cognitive_demand: transforming a quantity that is stored squared

archetypes.label: a circle both translated and resized, and the equation of the result
archetypes.given: a circle in standard form, a translation, and a diameter multiplier
archetypes.find: the equation of the new circle
archetypes.transformation: shift both coordinates and square the scaled radius
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the multiplier is stated on the DIAMETER and applies to the radius, then squares
archetypes.wrong_route: apply the multiplier to the stored constant, or halve it for the radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: the option set crosses the two centre choices with the two constant choices
archetypes.cognitive_demand: two independent transformations, one of them squared

archetypes.label: an equation assembled from a centre and a symbolic radius
archetypes.given: a centre and a radius written as a coefficient times a symbol
archetypes.transformation: negate the centre coordinates into the shifts and square the whole radius
archetypes.hidden_relationship: squaring a product squares BOTH factors, coefficient and symbol alike
archetypes.wrong_route: square the coefficient only, or square the symbol only
archetypes.distractor_basis: each half of the radius squared on its own, and neither
archetypes.cognitive_demand: squaring a product rather than a number

archetypes.label: the slope of a tangent, from the radius to the point of contact
archetypes.given: a centre and a point of tangency
archetypes.transformation: take the slope of the radius and its negative reciprocal
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, which is the only fact needed
archetypes.wrong_route: report the radius slope, or invert without negating
archetypes.distractor_basis: the radius slope, its reciprocal, and its negation
archetypes.cognitive_demand: one perpendicularity fact applied in the right direction

archetypes.label: a coordinate of the point of tangency, from the tangent slope
archetypes.given: a centre, a tangent slope, and one coordinate of the contact point
archetypes.transformation: the radius has the negative reciprocal slope; write it through the centre and solve
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the perpendicularity runs backwards here, from the tangent to the radius
archetypes.wrong_route: use the tangent slope for the radius, or drop the negation
archetypes.distractor_basis: the coordinate from the un-negated slope, and from the un-inverted slope
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reversing a relation that is usually used forwards

archetypes.label: a diameter endpoint recovered from the centre
archetypes.given: one endpoint of a diameter and the circle equation with a symbolic centre
archetypes.transformation: the centre is the midpoint, so reflect the known endpoint through it
archetypes.hidden_relationship: both endpoints share an abscissa, so the diameter is vertical and only the ordinate moves
archetypes.wrong_route: take the difference rather than the reflection, or use the radius as the gap
archetypes.distractor_basis: the centre ordinate, the gap itself, and the endpoint reflected the wrong way
archetypes.cognitive_demand: a midpoint used in reverse

archetypes.label: the radius from two intercepts on one axis
archetypes.given: a centre and the two points where the circle meets an axis
archetypes.transformation: halve the gap between the intercepts for the half-chord, then use the right triangle with the centre offset
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the two intercepts are a chord, not a diameter, so the radius needs Pythagoras and not a halving
archetypes.wrong_route: halve the intercept gap and call it the radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: the half-chord, the centre offset, and their sum
archetypes.cognitive_demand: seeing a right triangle that is not drawn

archetypes.label: the circumference from an arc length and its degree measure
archetypes.given: an arc length and the central angle in degrees
archetypes.transformation: scale the arc by the ratio of a full turn to the given measure
archetypes.hidden_relationship: arc length is proportional to central angle, so the whole is the part times the reciprocal fraction
archetypes.wrong_route: multiply by the degree measure, or divide instead of multiplying
archetypes.distractor_basis: the arc length itself, and scalings by the wrong factor
archetypes.cognitive_demand: a proportion set up in the right direction

archetypes.label: the circumference as the sum of a minor and a major arc
archetypes.given: the lengths of the two arcs between the same two points
archetypes.transformation: add them
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the two arcs between two points partition the whole circle, so nothing else is needed
archetypes.wrong_route: take one arc, or their difference
archetypes.distractor_basis: each arc on its own, and their difference
archetypes.cognitive_demand: recognising a partition rather than reaching for a formula

archetypes.label: one arc of a circle cut by two diameters into arcs in a stated ratio
archetypes.given: a circumference and a ratio between two of the four arcs
archetypes.find: the length of a named arc
archetypes.transformation: use the diameters to pair opposite arcs as equal, then solve the ratio over a half circle
archetypes.hidden_relationship: two diameters make vertical arcs equal, so four arcs reduce to two unknowns
archetypes.wrong_route: divide the circumference by four, or apply the ratio to the whole circle
archetypes.distractor_basis: a quarter of the circumference, and the other arc of the pair
archetypes.cognitive_demand: exploiting a symmetry that is stated only through the word diameter

archetypes.label: the ratio of two circle areas from their radii
archetypes.given: two radii, each a coefficient times a shared symbol
archetypes.find: how many times one area is the other
archetypes.transformation: take the ratio of the radii and square it
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the shared symbol cancels, so the answer is a pure number however the radii are written
archetypes.wrong_route: report the radius ratio unsquared
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: squaring a ratio and trusting the symbol to cancel

archetypes.label: the total area of two circles, one given by radius and one by area
archetypes.given: one radius and one area
archetypes.transformation: square the radius for the first area and add
archetypes.hidden_relationship: one circle is already an area and must not be squared again
archetypes.wrong_route: square the given area, or add the radius to the area
archetypes.distractor_basis: the given area alone, the radius added to it, and the radius doubled
archetypes.cognitive_demand: noticing that the two givens are different kinds of quantity

archetypes.label: the area of a circle from its radius
archetypes.given: a radius
archetypes.transformation: square it
archetypes.hidden_relationship: none; the item tests whether the radius is squared rather than doubled
archetypes.wrong_route: double the radius, or halve it
archetypes.distractor_basis: the radius, twice the radius, and four times it
archetypes.cognitive_demand: one formula, chosen correctly

archetypes.label: the diameter from the circumference
archetypes.given: a circumference
archetypes.transformation: divide out the constant
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the circumference is the diameter times the constant, so the division is direct and no radius step is needed
archetypes.wrong_route: halve the result to give the radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: stopping at the asked quantity

archetypes.label: a coordinate on the unit circle at an angle exceeding a full turn
archetypes.given: a unit circle, a reference point, and a large angle in radians
archetypes.find: a coordinate of the terminal point
archetypes.transformation: reduce the angle modulo a full turn, then read the coordinate
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the angle is many turns plus a familiar one, so the whole item reduces to one reference value
archetypes.wrong_route: reduce by the wrong multiple, or read the other coordinate
archetypes.distractor_basis: the other coordinate, and both with the sign flipped
archetypes.cognitive_demand: a modular reduction before any trigonometry

archetypes.label: which large angle measure reaches a stated point on the unit circle
archetypes.given: a unit circle and a terminal point on an axis
archetypes.find: a possible angle measure in radians
archetypes.transformation: find the base angle, then add whole turns and test the options
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the point is on the negative x-axis, so any odd multiple of a half turn works and the options differ by parity
archetypes.wrong_route: accept an even multiple, or use a quarter-turn base
archetypes.distractor_basis: even multiples of the half turn, and whole multiples of a full turn
archetypes.cognitive_demand: parity reasoning over a periodic quantity

archetypes.label: a trigonometric ratio read off a point on the unit circle
archetypes.given: a unit circle and a point with radical coordinates
archetypes.find: a ratio of the trigonometric functions of the angle
archetypes.transformation: identify the coordinates as cosine and sine and form the ratio
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the radical denominators are identical and cancel, so the answer is a ratio of the numerators
archetypes.wrong_route: invert the ratio, or drop a sign from a negative coordinate
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reading coordinates as function values

archetypes.label: the rate of change of a scaled circumference function
archetypes.given: a function giving a fraction of a circumference, and an increment in the radius
archetypes.find: the resulting increment in the function
archetypes.transformation: multiply the increment by the coefficient of the radius
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the function is linear in the radius, so the increment depends on the step and not on where it starts
archetypes.wrong_route: evaluate at the increment instead of scaling by it, or drop the fraction
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: treating a geometric formula as a linear function

archetypes.label: a length ratio in an equilateral triangle on a diameter
archetypes.given: a figure with a diameter, an equilateral triangle on it, and a perpendicular foot
archetypes.find: the ratio of one segment to the radius
archetypes.transformation: use the equilateral height relation against the radius
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the perpendicular from the vertex is the triangle height, and the radius is half the side
archetypes.wrong_route: use the side rather than half of it, or the wrong surd
archetypes.distractor_basis: the other common surd, and each surd reduced by one
archetypes.cognitive_demand: relating two figures that share only a segment

archetypes.label: a segment ratio from two perpendicular chords, one of them a diameter
archetypes.given: a figure with two chords meeting at right angles, one segment length, and the diameter
archetypes.find: the ratio into which one chord is divided
archetypes.transformation: use the intersecting-chord product with the perpendicular bisection, then solve the quadratic in the two parts
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the diameter perpendicular to a chord bisects it, so the product of the parts is the square of the given half-chord
archetypes.wrong_route: take the parts as equal, or use the diameter as a chord part
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable; the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: two circle theorems chained into a quadratic

archetypes.label: the volume of a named solid from its stated dimensions
archetypes.given: a solid and its dimensions
archetypes.transformation: substitute into the volume formula for that solid
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the formula carries a fraction for cones and pyramids and none for prisms and cylinders, and the option set is built on that difference
archetypes.wrong_route: use the diameter as the radius, or omit the fractional factor
archetypes.distractor_basis: the volume with the diameter used as the radius, without the fraction, and with the radius unsquared
archetypes.cognitive_demand: choosing one formula and substituting into it correctly

archetypes.label: a dimension recovered from a stated volume
archetypes.given: a volume and all but one dimension
archetypes.transformation: divide the volume by the rest of the formula
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the constant cancels when it appears on both sides, so the arithmetic is smaller than it looks
archetypes.wrong_route: multiply where the division belongs, or drop the fractional factor
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable where the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: running a formula backwards

archetypes.label: the surface area of a solid from its dimensions
archetypes.given: a solid and its dimensions
archetypes.transformation: sum the faces, counting each one the right number of times
archetypes.hidden_relationship: a face count is the whole item: an open box has five, a prism has three pairs, a pyramid has a base and its lateral faces
archetypes.wrong_route: count a missing face, or use a slant height where a perpendicular height is meant
archetypes.distractor_basis: not applicable where the response is student-produced
archetypes.cognitive_demand: enumerating faces without a picture

archetypes.label: a dimension recovered from a surface area
archetypes.given: a surface area and a relation between two dimensions
archetypes.transformation: substitute the relation into the surface formula and solve the quadratic
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the relation turns a two-variable formula into one quadratic, and only the positive root is a length
archetypes.wrong_route: take the negative root, or drop a term of the surface formula
archetypes.distractor_basis: the other root, and roots from a surface formula missing its ends
archetypes.cognitive_demand: a formula inverted through a quadratic

archetypes.label: the height of a pyramid from its total and lateral surface areas
archetypes.given: a total surface area and the combined area of the lateral faces
archetypes.transformation: subtract to get the base, take its side, get the slant height from a lateral face, then use the right triangle
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the slant height is not the height; the two differ by the half-side through Pythagoras
archetypes.wrong_route: report the slant height as the height
archetypes.distractor_basis: the slant height, the half-side, and the full side
archetypes.cognitive_demand: three chained steps where the second-last looks like the answer

archetypes.label: a lateral face of a square-based prism from its volume and base area
archetypes.given: a volume and the area of the square base
archetypes.find: the area of one lateral face, or the height
archetypes.transformation: take the side from the base area, the height from the volume, and multiply
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the base area gives the side only after a square root, which the option set punishes skipping
archetypes.wrong_route: use the base area as the side, or report the height
archetypes.distractor_basis: the height alone, the total lateral area, and the base area reused
archetypes.cognitive_demand: two extractions before the multiplication

archetypes.label: the total volume of two solids joined at a face
archetypes.given: a figure of two solids sharing a circular base, with a total height
archetypes.transformation: split the total height into the two parts and add the two volumes
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the hemisphere height is the radius, so the cone height is what remains of the total
archetypes.wrong_route: use the total height for both parts, or the diameter as the radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: each volume alone, and the sum with the total height used twice
archetypes.cognitive_demand: decomposing a figure before any formula applies

archetypes.label: the space in one solid not occupied by another inside it
archetypes.given: a cube and an inscribed sphere
archetypes.transformation: subtract the sphere from the cube
archetypes.hidden_relationship: the sphere touching each face means its diameter is the cube edge, which is stated twice over
archetypes.wrong_route: subtract the wrong way, or use the edge as the sphere radius
archetypes.distractor_basis: each volume alone, and the difference with the radius doubled
archetypes.cognitive_demand: reading an inscribed relation as an equality of two lengths

archetypes.label: the area of a similar figure under a stated linear scale
